questions.stem: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern protectorates of Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: On 1 January 1914 Sir Frederick Lugard united the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria with the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria. 1861 is the annexation of Lagos; 1960 is independence; 1963 is the Republican Constitution.

distractorRationale.a: 1861 marks the British annexation of Lagos Colony, not amalgamation of North and South
distractorRationale.d: 1963 is the year Nigeria became a republic

questions.stem: Indirect rule succeeded more in Northern Nigeria than in the East mainly because

options.text: the East had no people living there in 1914
the North already had a centralised emirate hierarchy which colonial officers could use
Easterners requested warrant chiefs in a referendum
the British never appointed residents in the North

questions.explanation: Indirect rule needs an existing ruler to work through. Emirates supplied emirs, district heads and alkali courts. Most Igbo communities were acephalous, so the British invented warrant chiefs who lacked legitimacy — a failure illustrated by the Aba Women's Riot of 1929.

distractorRationale.a: The East was densely populated; the problem was political structure, not emptiness
distractorRationale.c: Warrant chiefs were a colonial imposition, not a popular request
distractorRationale.d: Residents and district officers were the British supervisors of indirect rule in the North

questions.stem: Herbert Macaulay is regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism because he

options.text: became the first Prime Minister in 1960
founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party and led early organised opposition to colonial policy
commanded the West African Frontier Force

questions.explanation: Macaulay formed the NNDP in 1923 to contest the new Lagos elective seats under the Clifford Constitution, used newspapers and petitions against colonial measures, and later became president of the NCNC. He died in 1946, so he was neither Prime Minister nor a framer of the 1999 Constitution.

distractorRationale.a: The first Prime Minister was Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
distractorRationale.c: The WAFF was a colonial military formation, not Macaulay's organisation
distractorRationale.d: The 1999 Constitution was produced decades after his death

questions.stem: Which of the following was a cause of Nigerian nationalism?

options.text: Racial discrimination and the exclusion of educated Nigerians from real power
The creation of the African Union in 2002
The introduction of the naira in the Fourth Republic
Nigeria's membership of OPEC in the 1990s

questions.explanation: Educated Nigerians met a colour bar in the civil service, clubs and promotions. Combined with Western education, wartime experience, the Atlantic Charter, economic grievances and a nationalist press, that discrimination produced organised demand for self-government. The AU, the modern naira story and later OPEC politics are not causes of colonial-era nationalism.

distractorRationale.b: The AU was launched in 2002, forty-two years after independence
distractorRationale.c: Currency reforms of the republics did not cause anti-colonial nationalism
distractorRationale.d: OPEC membership is a post-independence oil-policy fact, not a cause of nationalism

questions.stem: Match the nationalist with the correct association: Azikiwe, Awolowo and Ahmadu Bello were leading figures respectively in the
questions.explanation: Azikiwe was the dominant figure of the NCNC; Awolowo founded and led the Action Group; Ahmadu Bello led the Northern People's Congress. Swapping those three is one of the most expensive mistakes in a Government paper. NNDP is Macaulay; PDP and APC belong to the Fourth Republic.

distractorRationale.c: NNDP is Macaulay; SDP is a Third Republic party; NYM was a 1930s youth movement, not Bello's party
distractorRationale.d: PDP, APC and APGA are Fourth Republic parties

questions.stem: The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) was formed in 1934 and the NCNC in 1944.
questions.explanation: True. The NYM (1934) was the first broader nationalist platform after the Lagos-based NNDP. The NCNC was founded in 1944 with Herbert Macaulay as president and Nnamdi Azikiwe as secretary. Those two dates sit between Clifford (1922) and the Macpherson Constitution (1951) on the standard timeline.

distractorRationale.b: Swapping 1934 and 1944, or confusing NYM with NNDP (1923), is the usual error
